note: GATE-COMMIT HAS A WARM FLOOR OF ~110-155s ON ambrose, NOT the 10-16s CLAUDE.md documents for a no-source-change run, and the cold-then-warm pair is reproducible. Aggregated from the ledger rather than reasoned about: grep for the gate-commit label in docs/timings.md, wall_s is FIELD 4 not field 3 (field 3 is the label, which is why a naive awk gives every row 0.0 and a mean of zero). Per host over 738 rows: MacBookPro n=663 min=2.1 mean=96.2 max=3857.6; ambrose n=32 min=6.6 mean=140.6 max=547.7; lefford n=34 min=3.9 mean=57.5 max=189.0; Greyjoy n=9 min=33.3 mean=219.3 max=630.2. THE COLD/WARM PAIR, same commit, back to back on ambrose: the-scour 454.147 then 110.271; the-leat 239.083 then 155.618; the-forebay 547.659 then 115.070 with no source change between. So a first gate in a freshly taken or freshly absorbed worktree pays 4-5x, and the second run is the real number. WHAT THE cpu_ratio SAYS: cold runs sit at 2.84-2.88 (parallel build) while warm runs sit at 0.71-0.98, i.e. the warm floor is SERIAL work, not tests -- the subfloor tier itself ran 483 tests in 12.045s inside a 115s wall. So roughly 100s of a warm gate-commit on this host is something single-threaded ahead of the tests, and scoping tests cannot touch it. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: do not budget 10-16s for a docs-only or scripts-only commit on this box, and do not read a 500s first gate as a defect in the change under test -- take a second reading before diagnosing. This is the same lesson the census cost paragraph in CLAUDE.md already teaches for a different label: read the number from the ledger, not from prose, and note which host the row belongs to.
